findings.message: Commit e938c197 is meant to make the outlook copy say six months everywhere, but it only fixed sections-plan.ts and Stats.tsx. The model still reads the old window in `pulseDescription`: 'capacity vs demand for the next five months, who is over-allocated and the bench for the next three'. Both cards now use SPAN = 6 (pulse-allocation.ts). The same stale count is in allocations' `get_load_summary` description ('Per month (the five shown)', modules/allocations/mcp-views.ts), although gridFor now returns six months. Fix: take both descriptions from the one window constant.
findings.scenario: A user asks 'who is over-allocated?'. get_delivery_pulse returns six months, including someone over 100% in month 5. Because the tool says 'next three', the bot answers 'nobody in the next three months' or mislabels the period.

findings.message: Commit 835d17ef adds the 24-month cap to allocate_only but no test that drives it. Add a table-driven test through the allocate_only tool or service: exactly 24 months accepted, 25 months refused on `through`, a range crossing years refused. It must fail without the new refine.
findings.scenario: Delete the new .refine and every allocations test still passes.

findings.message: Commit cfb81400 makes a project report refuse when Delivery or Allocations is off, but no test covers it. Add a variant test with reportsDb that switches off each module in turn. Cover export_report with project set while Delivery is off, then while Allocations is off (each refused with the new message), and with both on (a report is built).
findings.scenario: Remove the hasModule line and no test fails.

findings.message: Commit aefe7982 fixes a B3 defect: a failed list_allocations read looked the same as 'nothing unplanned'. It ships no test. Add a test with three cases: the grid read throws (the text says the plan couldn't be read), the grid has unplanned lines (they are listed), and the grid has none (no note). Keeping the message logic in lib/take-action.ts would make it testable.
findings.scenario: Revert the `${grid ? "" : ...}` change and no test fails.

findings.message: The standing branch of setAllocation returns early with an AllocationSet payload that has no `over`, `personUserId`, `project`, `month`, `total` or `byUser`, and it emits no monthSettled events. Both PM notification rules match on `when: { over: true|false }` and fill their templates from those fields, so a standing set or end never notifies the project's PM. Ending a standing allocation that fixed an over-allocation also never clears the urgent notification. Fix: run loadOf over the months written or removed, build the same payload as the month path, and emit monthSettled.
findings.scenario: An Admin sets Kasun Dias on CON at 60% until further notice while he is at 50% elsewhere. His total is 110%, yet CON's PM gets no 'is at 110%' notification. A one-month allocate with the same values would send it.

findings.message: allocationCards ignores its `month` and `today` parameters and builds its window from `new Date()`. The away card uses Reports' pinned `today` from settingsOf, and the report month can be behind the calendar (the chat rules say so). So the capacity and over-allocation cards follow a different clock from the rest of the report. Fix: build the window from the report's today or month (windowMonths(new Date(today), SPAN)), as the away card does.
findings.scenario: export_report kind delivery for month 2026-08 still shows capacity and over-allocation for Nov 2026 to Apr 2027, next to an August utilisation table. On the demo tenant pinned to 2026-10-16, the pulse capacity months follow the real date, not October.

findings.message: When month is left out, propose and note default it to windowMonths(new Date(),1)[0] when the card is made. run works out the same default again when the card is confirmed, and the stored card input carries no month. If the month changes between drafting and confirming, the write goes to a month the card never showed. Fix: write the defaulted month into the input before the card is stored, so run uses that pinned value.
findings.scenario: The card is drafted on 30 Nov and reads 'Add Kasun to CON · 50% in November'. It is confirmed on 1 Dec and writes the December row.

findings.message: The refusal text 'This report link isn't yours or is no longer valid…' is copied in the route, and modules/reports/server/export-slot.ts exports it as NOT_YOURS. The two copies can drift apart. Have the slot answer for the missing-handle case too, or move the text into @amax/core slots.
The README still describes capacity vs demand as 'next five months' and over-allocated/bench as 'next three months'. The code and the six-months copy fix now use six months. Update the doc to match.

The aefe7982 fix only covers the case where list_allocations throws. notPlanned still returns [] when the person isn't in the grid (outside the viewer's HR scope) or the month isn't in the window. That empty list means both 'everything is planned' and 'could not tell', so the note about unplanned projects is dropped silently. Return null or an 'unknown' state from notPlanned and show the 'couldn't be read' sentence for it too. No table-driven test covers the fixed path, the missing-person path or the missing-month path (B2).
findings.scenario: A PM presses Take action on a suggestion for someone who is hidden by their HR scope. The grid loads, notPlanned returns [], and the text claims nothing is unplanned without saying the plan couldn't be checked.

findings.message: propose skips overCheck whenever standing is present, so the 'Are you sure?' step depends on whether the model includes standing:false. Any model or MCP call can avoid the over-100% question by adding that field. Tell a card edit apart from a model call some other way, for example a flag the chat engine sets on a card edit.
findings.scenario: The model calls allocate {…percent:100, standing:false} for someone at 100%. The card is made without the model being told to ask first.

findings.message: onLeaver passes String(event.payload.leftOn). A missing field becomes the string "undefined", which passes z.string() and makes addMonths throw a RangeError, so the handler fails and retries with no clear reason. Validate personId and leftOn as a date, and refuse with a plain message.
findings.scenario: An hr.person.left payload without leftOn makes the handler throw 'Invalid time value' on every retry.
